questions.question: Higher workability of concrete is required if the structure is
questions.explanation: Higher workability ensures that concrete flows easily around congested reinforcement and fills thin or heavily reinforced sections completely without honeycombing[cite: 3].

questions.question: Pick up the correct statement form the following:

options.a: higher workability indicates unexpected increase in the moisture content
options.b: higher workability indicates deficiency of sand
options.c: if the concrete mix is dry, the slump is zero
options.d: concrete mix having zero slump, is unsuitable for high strength

questions.explanation: All statements correctly describe various aspects of workability, moisture variation, and slump characteristics in concrete mixes[cite: 3].

questions.question: The maximum thickness of concrete floor of a cement warehouse, is
questions.explanation: A standard concrete floor thickness of 15 cm is generally recommended and sufficient for cement warehouses to prevent moisture dampness from the ground[cite: 3].

questions.question: The shuttering of a hall measuring 4m x 5m can be removed after
questions.explanation: According to standard codes (like IS 456), shuttering/formwork to slabs (spanning up to 4.5m) can be removed after 7 days[cite: 3].

questions.question: Pick up the correct statement from the following

options.a: there should not be any loss of cement from the charged drum of the mixer
options.b: cement should be mixed for at least one minute
options.c: 10% of water is placed in the rotating drum before adding dry material
options.d: 10% of water is added after placing the other ingredients in the drum

questions.explanation: All these are standard good practices in batching and mixing concrete in a mixer drum[cite: 3].

questions.question: If the effective working time is 7 hours and per batch time of concrete mixer capacity, is...
questions.explanation: Based on standard mixer output calculations where total output equals working hours multiplied by batches per hour and mixer capacity[cite: 3].

questions.question: The main object of compaction of concrete is

options.c: to provide intimate contact between the concrete and embedded materials

questions.explanation: Compacting concrete removes entrapped air voids, maximizes density, and ensures proper bond with reinforcement and embedded items[cite: 3].

questions.question: Non-uniform compaction may cause the concrete
questions.explanation: Inadequate or non-uniform compaction leaves localized air pockets, leading to porosity, non-homogeneity, and weak zones[cite: 3].

questions.question: The compaction of concrete, improves
questions.explanation: Eliminating voids directly enhances density, compressive strength, and overall durability[cite: 3].

questions.question: The final operation of finishing floors, is known
questions.explanation: Trowelling is the final smoothing operation performed on concrete floors after floating[cite: 3].

questions.question: The operation of removing humps and hollows of uniform concrete surface, is known as
questions.explanation: Screeding strikes off excess concrete and removes surface irregularities, leveling humps and hollows[cite: 3].

questions.question: The ratio of the length and breadth of wooden float, is
questions.explanation: Standard proportioning for wooden floats used in finishing gives a length-to-breadth ratio around 7.5[cite: 3].

questions.question: Construction joints are provided

options.a: where BM and SF are small
options.b: where it is supported by another member
options.c: at 18 m apart in huge structures
options.d: in concrete wall at sill level of windows

questions.explanation: All listed conditions and locations are standard practice for placing construction joints[cite: 3].

questions.question: The surface where two successive placements of concrete meet, is known as
questions.explanation: A construction joint marks the boundary where fresh concrete is placed against previously hardened concrete[cite: 3].

questions.question: A construction joint is provided where

options.c: it is supported by other member

questions.explanation: Construction joints are planned at locations of minimum stress (low bending moment and shear force) or support locations[cite: 3].

questions.question: Horizontal construction joins in concrete walls are generally provided at
questions.explanation: Horizontal joints in walls are typically located at architectural lines like soffit levels, sill levels, and floor levels[cite: 3].

questions.question: Pick up the correct statement from the following:

options.a: construction joints in columns are provided a few cm below the junction of beam
options.b: construction joints in columns are provided at the bottom haunching
options.c: construction joints in beam and slabs are provided within middle third
options.d: construction joints are generally provided in positions subjected to least shear force

questions.explanation: Each of these statements correctly outlines standard code provisions for positioning structural construction joints[cite: 3].

questions.question: Joints in concrete structures, are provided

options.a: to reduce the tensile stresses likely to be developed due to evaporation of water
options.b: to minimize the change in the dimensions of the slab

questions.explanation: Joints accommodate volume changes, control cracking, and relieve tensile stresses caused by shrinkage and temperature variations[cite: 3].

questions.question: Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structures exceeds
questions.explanation: Structures exceeding roughly 40m to 45m in length require expansion joints to prevent thermal cracking[cite: 3].

questions.question: According to the recommendations of IS:456-2000, expansion joints

options.a: are provided where plane changes abruptly
options.b: are provided to ensure minimum resistance
options.d: do not carry reinforcement across them

questions.explanation: All given guidelines conform to IS:456 provisions regarding expansion joint detailing[cite: 3].

questions.question: Construction joints are generally provided in concrete
questions.explanation: Construction joints are widely utilized in pavements, walls, and long lining works where continuous casting is impossible[cite: 3].

questions.question: Pick up the correct statement from the following:

options.a: construction joins are necessarily planned for their locations
options.b: expansion joints are provided to accommodate thermal expansion
options.c: construction joints are provided to control shrinkage cracks
options.d: expansion joints need not be provided in foundation concrete

questions.explanation: All statements accurately describe the principles of structural joint planning[cite: 3].

questions.question: The main purpose of concrete design mix is

options.b: mixing the concrete in better way

questions.explanation: Design mix aims to optimize proportions to achieve required strength and durability with maximum economy[cite: 3].

questions.question: Generally nominal mix is done by volume while design mix is done by
questions.explanation: Nominal mixes use volumetric batching, whereas designed mixes require precise weight batching of ingredients[cite: 3].

questions.question: Pick up the correct statement from the following:

options.a: the free water is the amount of water added while mixing and the amount held on the surface of the aggregates prior to mixing
options.b: the total water is the free water and the amount actually absorbed by the aggregate

questions.explanation: Both definitions correctly account for surface moisture (free water) and absorption characteristics of aggregates[cite: 3].

questions.question: If the average compressive strength is 4000 kg/cm2 and standard deviation is 500, coefficient of variation is
questions.explanation: Numerical Solution: Coefficient of Variation (CV) = (Standard Deviation / Mean) * 100 = (500 / 4000) * 100 = 12.5%[cite: 3].

questions.question: The risk of segregation is more for

options.b: larger proportion of maximum size aggregate

questions.explanation: Wet mixes, large maximum aggregate sizes, and gap or coarse gradings all increase the tendency of cement paste and aggregates to separate (segregation)[cite: 3].

questions.question: The process by which fresh cement concrete is compacted to remove the air bubbles known as
questions.explanation: Compaction is specifically the process of expelling entrapped air from fresh concrete[cite: 3].

questions.question: Maturity of concrete means

options.c: sum of product of temperature & time

questions.explanation: Maturity is quantified as the cumulative product of curing temperature and time (degree-hours or degree-days)[cite: 3].

questions.question: Gypsum is used as admixture in concrete to increase the property of concrete
questions.explanation: Gypsum acts primarily as a set-retarder in cement manufacturing and concrete mixes[cite: 3].

questions.question: Calcium chloride is used as admixture in concrete to increase the property of concrete
questions.explanation: Calcium chloride is a well-known accelerating admixture that speeds up setting and early strength gain[cite: 3].

questions.question: Calcium chloride as an accelerating admixture is not recommended for use with
questions.explanation: Calcium chloride can cause adverse chemical reactions and loss of strength or corrosion when used with high alumina cement[cite: 3].

questions.question: To improve the certain properties of concrete, admixture is used in concrete at the time of
questions.explanation: Admixtures are typically added during the mixing process to ensure uniform dispersion throughout the batch[cite: 3].

questions.question: An admixture...

options.a: is a substitute for good concreting practice
options.b: offers improvement not economically attained by adjusting mix proportions
options.d: is beneficial to the properties of concrete when used in large quantities

questions.explanation: Admixtures are used to achieve specific performance improvements that are otherwise uneconomical or difficult via mix adjustments alone[cite: 3].

questions.question: An admixture could be used to
questions.explanation: Different types of admixtures can accelerate setting, increase strength, or improve workability[cite: 3].

questions.question: An accelerator shortens all of the following except
questions.explanation: Accelerators shorten setting time, curing period, and formwork stripping time, but they do not reduce/shorten the ultimate strength of concrete[cite: 3].

questions.question: Addition of retarder to concrete decreases all of the following except
questions.explanation: Retarders slow down hydration and strength development rates, whereas water-cement ratio is managed independently based on mix design[cite: 3].

questions.question: Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
questions.explanation: Specialized admixtures can fulfill each of these specialized functions depending on their chemical formulation[cite: 3].

questions.question: Gel space ratio is defined as the ratio of

options.a: volume of hydrated cement paste to the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores
options.b: the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores to volume of hydrated cement
options.c: both a) and b) of above

questions.explanation: Gel-space ratio is the ratio of the volume of hydrated cement gel to the sum of the volumes of gel and capillary pores[cite: 3].

questions.question: Find the gel space ratio of concrete with following data: cement = 50 kg. Weight of water = 20 kg
questions.explanation: Numerical Solution: Using Powers' gel-space ratio formula for fully hydrated cement with given water-cement proportion yields approximately 0.91[cite: 3].

questions.question: The minimum grade of high strength concrete is
questions.explanation: According to standard structural engineering classifications, high-strength concrete typically starts from grade M50[cite: 3].

questions.question: The type of aggregates not suitable for high strength concrete and for pavements to tension, is
questions.explanation: Flaky and elongated aggregates result in poor interlocking, high void content, and low strength, making them unsuitable[cite: 3].

questions.question: The aggregate used for high strength concrete is
questions.explanation: Angular aggregates provide superior interlocking and frictional resistance, essential for high-strength concrete[cite: 3].

questions.question: To obtain a very high strength concrete, use very fine grained
questions.explanation: Heavy, dense, fine-grained mineral aggregates like magnetite are used for specialized high-strength and radiation-shielding concretes[cite: 3].

questions.question: Prestress is imparted to concrete by bearing in
questions.explanation: Prestressing force is transferred via bond in pre-tensioning and via end-anchorage bearing plates in post-tensioning[cite: 3].

questions.question: The minimum grade of concrete for pre-tensioned member is
questions.explanation: IS 1343 specifies M25 as the minimum concrete grade for pre-tensioned prestressed concrete members[cite: 3].

questions.question: The mix proportion of cement mortar used in the joints in precast prestressed member is
questions.explanation: A rich cement mortar mix of 1:1 is typically used for jointing precast prestressed elements to ensure high strength and bonding[cite: 3].

questions.question: The diameter of high tensile steel tendons used is
questions.explanation: High tensile steel wires and tendons commonly range between 5 mm to 8 mm in diameter[cite: 3].

questions.question: The minimum clear spacing for single wires used in pre-tension system is

options.a: 2 times the diameter of wire and max size of aggregate whichever is greater
options.b: 3 times the diameter of wire and max size of aggregate whichever is greater
options.c: 2 times the diameter of wire and 1.5 times max size of aggregate whichever is greater
options.d: 3 times the diameter of wire and 1.5 times max size of aggregate whichever is greater

questions.explanation: Standard code provisions require clear spacing to be at least 3 times wire diameter or 1.5 times maximum aggregate size, whichever is greater[cite: 3].

questions.question: The minimum clear spacing of non-grouped cables or large bars shall be

options.b: maximum size of cable or bar
options.c: 5 mm plus maximum size of aggregate

questions.explanation: Clear spacing rules for non-grouped cables take the maximum of these criteria to ensure proper consolidation[cite: 3].

questions.question: The minimum clear horizontal spacing between groups of cables or ducts of grouped cables shall be greater of

options.a: 30 mm or 5 mm more than maximum size of aggregate
options.b: 40 mm or 5 mm more than maximum size of aggregate
options.c: 30 mm or maximum size of aggregate
options.d: 40 mm or maximum size of aggregate

questions.explanation: Horizontal duct spacing must accommodate aggregate flow around groups per standard prestressed design codes[cite: 3].

questions.question: The minimum clear vertical spacing between groups of cables or ducts of grouped cables shall be
questions.explanation: Vertical clearance requirements between cable groups are specified as 40 mm to permit adequate grout and concrete placement[cite: 3].

questions.question: The grouting of ducts in post-tensioned prestressed concrete causes
questions.explanation: Grouting protects tendons from corrosion, improves bond between steel and concrete, and enhances structural rigidity[cite: 3].

questions.question: A parabolic tendon in prestressed beam causes an equivalent balancing
questions.explanation: A parabolic profile exerts a uniform upward transverse load opposing gravity loads across the span[cite: 3].

questions.question: An increase in strain in a concrete member at constant stress is called
questions.explanation: Creep is defined as the time-dependent increase in strain under sustained constant stress[cite: 3].

questions.question: Strain in concrete at zero stress is called
questions.explanation: Volume changes occurring due to moisture loss without external load application represent drying shrinkage[cite: 3].

questions.question: In case of prestressed concrete, prestressing force is
questions.explanation: Prestressing introduces initial internal compressive stresses into the concrete section to counteract tensile stresses[cite: 3].

questions.question: In case of prestressed concrete

options.a: load carrying capacity of member increases
options.b: quantity of concrete is saved for same grade
options.c: quantity of steel is saved for same grade

questions.explanation: Prestressing optimizes material utilization, reducing dead weight and material quantities while improving load capacity[cite: 3].

questions.question: Light weight concrete is prepared by

options.b: formation of air void in concrete by omitting sand
options.c: formation of air voids in cement paste by the substances causing foam

questions.explanation: Lightweight concrete can be produced using lightweight aggregates, gas-forming agents, or by omitting fine aggregate (no-fines)[cite: 3].

questions.question: Light weight concrete is used in
questions.explanation: It is predominantly utilized in non-load-bearing partitions and thermal insulation applications[cite: 3].

questions.question: To obtain a light weight concrete the types of aggregate used are
questions.explanation: Pumice is a porous, lightweight volcanic aggregate used specifically for producing lightweight concrete[cite: 3].

questions.question: A concrete in which dry coarse aggregate first packed... and cement sand mortar injected is known as
questions.explanation: Pre-packed (or prepacked/aggregate) concrete involves placing coarse aggregate first and injecting grout/mortar into voids[cite: 3].

questions.question: The ferrocement is a composite material obtained by

options.a: random disposal of short, discontinuous fibres in conventional concrete
options.b: reinforcing the cement mortar with steel fibres in the form of wire mesh
options.c: blending ferrous compounds in ordinary Portland cement

questions.explanation: Ferrocement consists of rich cement mortar reinforced with multiple layers of continuous wire mesh[cite: 3].

questions.question: The cement sand ratio in the ferrocement matrix should not be leaner than
questions.explanation: Ferrocement matrix requires a rich mortar mix, typically not leaner than 1:1.5 cement-to-sand ratio[cite: 3].

questions.question: The volume of reinforcement in ferrocement (percent) normally varies between
questions.explanation: The volume fraction of wire mesh reinforcement in ferrocement normally ranges from 2% to 5%[cite: 3].

questions.question: The water cement ratio for ferrocement mix should be
questions.explanation: A low water-cement ratio (less than 0.35) is maintained in ferrocement to ensure high strength and impermeability[cite: 3].

questions.question: What is the process of smoothening the surface of newly placed concrete with... called?
questions.explanation: Floating levels and smoothens the surface of freshly placed concrete[cite: 3].

questions.question: If water cement ratio is more,

options.a: the durability of the concrete will be more
options.b: the durability of the concrete will be less
options.c: the durability of the concrete will not be affected

questions.explanation: Higher water-cement ratios increase porosity and permeability, thereby decreasing durability[cite: 3].

questions.question: Low water-cement ratio in concrete:
questions.explanation: A low water-cement ratio benefits strength, impermeability, and resistance to environmental weathering[cite: 3].

questions.question: To get ultra high strength concrete:

options.a: compaction by pressure and helical binding

questions.explanation: Ultra-high-strength concretes utilize advanced techniques such as reactive powders, high pressure compaction, and polymers[cite: 3].

questions.question: As compared to Ordinary Portland Cement, use of pozzolanic cement:
questions.explanation: Pozzolanic cement typically exhibits higher drying shrinkage compared to standard OPC mixes[cite: 3].

questions.question: Steel mould used for slump test is in the form of:
questions.explanation: The standard slump cone mould is shaped as a frustum of a cone[cite: 3].

questions.question: The interval for which the cement products remain in plastic condition is known as
questions.explanation: Setting time refers to the duration over which cement paste remains workable and plastic[cite: 3].

questions.question: The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1:3 cement:sand) after days test should not be less than:
questions.explanation: Standard 3-day or 7-day mortar cube strength requirements specify minimum thresholds (e.g., 175 kg/cm2 for 7 days in older specifications)[cite: 3].

questions.question: The concrete in which preliminary tests are preformed for designing the mix is called
questions.explanation: Controlled concrete relies on preliminary mix design tests to guarantee specified target strengths[cite: 3].

questions.question: Concreting should be stopped when temperature falls below...
questions.explanation: Standard specifications state that concreting should not proceed if ambient temperature drops below 4.5°C without special precautions[cite: 3].

questions.question: Humidity causes ... of cement in bag.
questions.explanation: Atmospheric moisture entering cement bags causes pre-hydration, lump formation, and decaying/spoiling of cement[cite: 3].

questions.question: The purpose of reinforcement in prestressed concrete is:

options.a: to impact initial compressive stress in concrete

questions.explanation: High-tensile steel tendons primarily resist tensile forces and introduce pre-compression[cite: 3].

questions.question: Reduction in aggregate cement ratio while keeping W/C ratio constant causes:
questions.explanation: Lowering aggregate-cement ratio means a richer mix (more paste content), which increases workability[cite: 3].

questions.question: Modulus of rupture of concrete is measure of:
questions.explanation: Modulus of rupture measures the flexural tensile strength of concrete beams[cite: 3].

questions.question: Slump test is done for
questions.explanation: The slump test is a standard method to measure the workability of fresh concrete[cite: 3].

questions.question: The durability of concrete is proportion to:
questions.explanation: Durability is inversely proportional to the water-cement ratio (lower water-cement ratio yields higher durability)[cite: 3].

questions.question: Plain cement concrete is strong in taking:
questions.explanation: Plain cement concrete has high compressive strength but is weak in tension and shear[cite: 3].

questions.question: The removal of excess air after placing concrete helps in increasing the strength of concrete by:
questions.explanation: Proper compaction removing entrapped air can boost concrete strength significantly (approx 20 to 30%)[cite: 3].

questions.question: The strength of concrete increase with decreases in:
questions.explanation: According to Abrams' law, strength increases as the water-cement ratio decreases[cite: 3].

questions.question: The cold bent test is conducted in a steel bar to determine:
questions.explanation: The cold bend test checks the ductility and capacity of steel reinforcement bars to bend without fracturing[cite: 3].

questions.question: As compared to ordinary Portland cement, use of pozzolanic cement:
questions.explanation: Pozzolanic cements tend to exhibit increased bleeding characteristics compared to standard OPC[cite: 3].

questions.question: For the same design load, the weight of concrete in a prestressed concrete as compared to ordinary reinforced concrete is less by:
questions.explanation: Prestressed concrete structural members require significantly less cross-sectional area and concrete weight (roughly 50% less) for identical loads[cite: 3].

questions.question: To determine the modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is
questions.explanation: Standard beam specimens for flexural strength tests measure 150 x 150 x 700 mm (or 100 x 100 x 500 mm depending on aggregate size)[cite: 3].

questions.question: The steel mould used for slump test is in the form of:
questions.explanation: The standard slump cone is a frustum of a cone[cite: 3].

questions.question: Expansive cement expands mostly during its:
questions.explanation: Expansive cement undergoes controlled expansion primarily during its final hardening and early curing stage[cite: 3].

questions.question: Soundness of the material means the resistance of the material against the effect of:
questions.explanation: In aggregate and material testing, soundness specifically denotes resistance to weathering actions like alternate freezing and thawing[cite: 3].

questions.question: What is a graded aggregate?

options.a: it has particles of all sizes
options.b: it has particles between 4 mm - 6 mm
options.c: it has particles between 10 mm - 15 mm
options.d: it has particles between 2 mm - 5 mm

questions.explanation: A well-graded aggregate contains particles of various sizes proportioned to minimize void space[cite: 3].

questions.question: Finer grinding of cement

options.a: affects only the early development of strength

questions.explanation: Finer cement increases surface area, accelerating early hydration and rate of strength gain[cite: 3].

questions.question: The individual variation between test strength of sample should not be more than
questions.explanation: Standard testing codes stipulate that individual cube strength results should not deviate by more than +/- 10% from the mean batch average[cite: 3].

questions.question: To obtain a very high strength concrete, use very fine grained:
questions.explanation: Magnetite is utilized as heavy, fine aggregate for specialized high-density/strength mixes[cite: 3].

questions.question: The percentage of voids in cement is approximately:
questions.explanation: Loose bulk cement typically contains approximately 35% air voids[cite: 3].

questions.question: The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as:
questions.explanation: Abrasion resistance measures an aggregate's ability to withstand surface wear and friction[cite: 3].

questions.question: For the construction of cement concrete floor the maximum permissible sizes of aggregate is:
questions.explanation: For thin concrete floor toppings, maximum aggregate size is restricted (typically 8 mm)[cite: 3].

questions.question: Age factor for permissible compressive stress in concrete after six months is:
questions.explanation: Age factors account for continuous strength gain beyond 28 days, reaching 1.15 at 6 months[cite: 3].

questions.question: Fineness of cement is measured in unit of:
questions.explanation: Fineness is expressed as specific surface area (e.g., $m^2/kg$ or $cm^2/g$), which relates to surface area per unit mass/volume[cite: 3].

questions.question: The cement-sand ratio used in the compressive strength test of cement as per the Standard Specification is:
questions.explanation: Standard cement mortar cube tests use a 1:3 cement-to-sand weight proportion[cite: 3].

questions.question: The initial setting time of lime-pozzolana, is:
questions.explanation: Lime-pozzolana mixes exhibit slower chemical reactions, having an initial setting time of 120 minutes[cite: 3].

questions.question: The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at a considerable depth front surface are called
questions.explanation: Plutonic rocks are intrusive igneous rocks formed by slow cooling of magma deep underground[cite: 3].

questions.question: Depending on the chemical composition and mechanical properties, iron may be classified as
questions.explanation: Iron-based engineering metals are classified into cast iron, wrought iron, and steel based on carbon content and properties[cite: 3].
